newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg's net beats forecasts, stock pops up.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg's net beats forecasts, stock pops up.

text.p: Kellogg Co. said Friday its net income more than doubled in the second quarter, sailing past Wall Street estimates and driving the cereal giant's stock up sharply.

Kellogg said gains in its share of the U.S. cereal market helped to push earnings to $163.6 million, or 79 cents a share, in the quarter. The returns easily outpaced profits of $78.1 million, or 37 cents a share, posted in last year's second quarter.
Kellogg's stock surged $4.375 to $96.25 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most actively traded issues at midday. It hit a 52-week high of $97.69 early in the day.
The second quarter results stood in sharp contrast to the company's year-ago performance, when a price war among leading U.S. cereal makers took a toll on Kellogg's bottom line.

"Wonderful. Well above expectations," said Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez, who had forecast Kellogg's earnings at 75 cents a share. "I have to believe that this shows that Kellogg is back on its feet," Ghez added.

Excluding one-time charges, Kellogg earned 83 cents a share, which beat an average forecast compiled by First Call of 73 cents a share and even outdid predictions made by a few analysts that it would match the 77 cents a share seen in the 1995 quarter.

The leader of the $9 billion U.S. cereal market said second-quarter sales rose 4 percent to $1.72 billion. Global sales volume climbed 14 percent following the acquisitition last December of Lender's Bagels. Excluding Lender's, volume rose 8 percent.

Kellogg said its domestic market share hit 33.8 percent in the quarter, continuing a steady improvement over the last several quarters. The company netted a 33.2 percent market share in the first quarter, 32.9 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, and 32.6 percent in the second and third quarters of last year.
Kellogg's convenience foods business, which includes Nutri-Grain bars, increased by a double-digit rate in the second quarter.

Battle Creek, Mich.-based Kellogg said its North American cereal volume grew in the quarter, but no specifics were provided. Growth was aided by its two newest cereals -- Honey Crunch Corn Flakes and Cocoa Frosted Flakes -- which control between 2 percent and 3 percent of the cereal market.
Kellogg also said it was extending its Rice Krispies line with the introduction Razzle Dazzle Rice Krispies cereal, which is expected to hit grocery stores nationwide Sept. 1.
"We still think we are in an exciting business category," Joseph Stewart, senior vice president of corporate affairs, said of the U.S. cereal industry.
He added that while the U.S. cereal industry overall is growing by about 1.4 percent, Kellogg expects it could grow at a rate of 2 percent "over time."
This would be below its historic growth rate of 3 percent, but an improvement from a relatively flat performance in 1996.
Kellogg said its second-quarter cereal volume was up in all four of its global operations areas -- North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
Stewart declined to say specifically if Kellogg expects to sustain the robust growth shown in the second quarter.
"We are confident in our long-term strategy and we're sticking to it long term," Stewart said.
Kellogg also announced a 2-for-1 stock split and increased its quarterly dividend to 22.5 cents a share from 21 cents a share.
